utterances.text: So if I understand your answer correctly, some of the changes you made on Tuesday were changes to comments that you made at the time you gave your statement but you realised last weekend you had made those comments without much thought, and you changed them; is that right?

utterances.speaker: PETAR PASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is partly correct. Some statements and some comments do not reflect my words but, rather, the words of either the interpreter or the investigator.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Just so it's clear to me, when you said it is partly correct, it's correct that some of the changes that you made were changes to comments you had made to the investigators that you realised last weekend you had given without much thought; is that right?

utterances.speaker: PETAR PASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, we're in difficulty this side of the courtroom. I believe I'm not the only one. We've got no transcript and so we can't make notes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, efforts to be reconnected are, at this moment, not successful.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Pasic, we're just having a technical difficulty.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I --

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: It's working again.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Pasic, if we looked at the -- if you looked at the statement that you gave on Tuesday, would you be able to identify now which of the changes you made were changes you made to statements that you had given to the investigators but that you had given without much thought? Would you be able to do this now?

utterances.speaker: PETAR PASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I perused the statement that I provided to the investigators, and I made my own corrections, and -- well, you can see the penultimate paragraph, the last paragraph, the military could stop the attack in villages. I travelled to Sibenik every day. These are all things which were not said by me. These are not my words.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: The reason I'm asking, Mr. Pasic, is because the statement that gave on Tuesday, for every single change that you made, the explanation that's given is that you didn't say that. And now it's clear from your evidence that some of the changes you made are changes to statements that you did in fact make but you realised you had given without much thought. My question is: Are you able to distinguish those two situations? Are you able to distinguish the statements that you gave that you said you didn't make, versus the ones you said you made but you didn't give much thought to?

utterances.speaker: PETAR PASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Which ones, Mr. Pasic? Which of the changes here in points 1 through 16 are changes that you made to statements that gave to the investigators without much thought?

utterances.speaker: PETAR PASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in every paragraph, there is an explanation as to what I said, as to what I didn't say as well. I did not say that lorries full of sheep were let through the check-points and that the lorries were driven by members of the Croatian military or the Croatian police. I didn't say that.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Mr. Pasic, my question is a little different. In every change in points 1 through 16 of this statement, it says that you're making the change because you didn't say that. But your evidence now is clear that some of the changes you made were changes to things you said but that you had said them without much thought. Do you understand the difference?

utterances.speaker: PETAR PASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And are you able to identify now the changes that reflect comments that you made to the investigators but you made without much thought?

utterances.speaker: PETAR PASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For example, the annex statement 1, it says that I didn't see the wounded and the killed. I'm telling you now that I never saw a dead body and especially I didn't see any when I return -- returned after Operation Storm. So this is simply not correct. In paragraph 2, here, as well, there are some things which reflect my words and some don't. Some do not reflect the corrections that I made.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Mr. Pasic, I -- I'm not sure I understand. Are you or are you not able to identify the specific changes in the statement you made on Tuesday that relate to comments you made to the investigators but you realised last weekend you made without much thought? Are you able to identify those specific changes or not?

utterances.speaker: PETAR PASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand you. I would like to understand you. In every additional statement, there is an explanation as to where the true -- the words were not correct and where there are supplements and additions which reflect my new view of the situation.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: In light of the witness's answers, I'm moving on to the next and final question that I have --

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: For you, Mr. Pasic, which again relates back to something that you said on Friday, when you confirmed that the song you referred to as Jure and Boban was the same song that's also known as Evo Zore, Evo Dana. Now Jure and Boban in that song, that refers to Jure Francetic and Rafael Boban who were commanders of the Black Legion which was a World War II Ustasha unit; is that right?

utterances.speaker: PETAR PASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that, but that song does not have to be tied only to them. Some of the words of that song may be incriminated [as interpreted] and only then lead to the phenomenon that can be tied to them as the high officials of the one-time regime.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Pasic, for answering my questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Gustafson. May I take it there must be some translation issue with the word "incriminated" in the last answer, "words of that song may be incriminated."

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: I think I heard "incriminating," at least in the English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, incriminating, yes. Yes, Mr. Kay -- well, Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: No, I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic, yes, you were not --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I wasn't just suggesting anything. I was just looking at the Chamber how the Chamber wished to proceed. That's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, unless the parties would -- it was announced by Mr. Misetic that he might need more time in cross-examination depending on what was raised by the Prosecution. Now, I don't know whether you formed any opinion about whether it would be appropriate to do it now, because most likely then at least there is a chance that Mr. Kay would, apart from his re-examination, then ask for further re-examination after your cross-examination, so therefore, it might be very practical to allow you first to add to your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: That's what I was thinking and that my friend Mr. Kay is -- I believe agrees with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then please proceed, Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Pasic.

utterances.speaker: PETAR PASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning, Counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I'd like to start off now with Jure i Boban. Now, I have to ask you a few questions about this. You were asked on Friday about where these -- this song was sung and I believe in the transcript of Friday's session it indicates you said there were three or four occasions and you named several singers on these occasions; one was Krunoslav Cigoj; the second was Kico Sladinac, I believe; and the third was --

utterances.speaker: PETAR PASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Hrid Matic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Hrid Matic. I'd like to recall -- I'd like to ask you: Do you recall, in fact, that Mr. Cigoj and Mr. Matic didn't appear at separate concerts but it was one concert?

utterances.speaker: PETAR PASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were separate concerts. They each had their own slot or their own guest appearance.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Let me -- let me show you a video.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Just one moment, Mr. President. This is 65 ter 1D2987.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Do you recall, first of all, a concert at the Knin castle on the 17th of October [sic], where various dignitaries were present including yourself, General Gotovina, General Forand, members of the ECMM and other international organisations? Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: PETAR PASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see anything on the screen. Where did that concert take place?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I believe it was at the fortress in Knin. Does that refresh your memory?

utterances.speaker: PETAR PASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that I did not attend that concert. On the day of the concert, I was visited by the prefect of Istria county, Mr. del Bianco, and as far as I can remember, I did not attend that particular event.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I may have misspoken. It was the 17th of August not the 17th of October.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I'll -- Mr. President, we'll play a short clip from the concert. We have the entire two-hour video, which I believe is now relevant and we will tender the entire two hours. But if we could play this clip and then we'll pause it at a certain moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is the issue what songs were sung or who was present?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Both.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Both.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then if you could limit yourself to portions of the video that would be sufficient to establish that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is there no -- I wonder whether there's any agreement possible on this text, songs, when, in the presence of whom. That seems to be the relatively simple issue.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this point I just can't say. I just got disclosed the transcripts. I have no idea what they reflect, whether they're complete, what the videos actually show. I'm just not in a position to -- to say anything at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's watch the video on strictly relevant portions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Pasic, do you recognise any persons in this shot that's on the screen at 17 seconds of this clip?

utterances.speaker: PETAR PASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, as I have already told you, I did not attend that event. I know that this a song from opera Zrinski, but I don't know whether this person, I can see on the clip is Mr. Cigoj. He is wearing a costume. But I know he is the one who performs that particular aria quite often.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Do you recognise -- first, I -- Mr. Cigoj would the person in the costume on the left, correct?

utterances.speaker: PETAR PASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is it your left or my left? As I'm looking at the screen, he is on my right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Pasic, grey or the costume with some red in it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Grey, a grey costume.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Do you recognise who the person is in the costume opposite?

utterances.speaker: PETAR PASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Would it surprise you to learn that, in fact, Mr. Cigoj is the person on the left, and the person on the right in the costume is, in fact, the Mr. Matic you refer to in your testimony?

utterances.speaker: PETAR PASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Quite possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Is it also quite possible, then, that in fact you're incorrect in saying that they were separate concerts but that in fact it was one concert where both Mr. Matic and Mr. Cigoj sang an opera together?

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm not sure there is a foundation for this. We have no idea how many concerts there were in total. The witness has said he wasn't at this concert.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I think this should have been done by the Prosecution in cross. I'm in cross now. I will go through it step by step with the witness, but let's start with the one concert that everyone can agree and that there is some foundation in the evidence of this trial took place, which is this concert.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, let's focus on what we see, and in view of the answers the witness is giving, let's not speculate too much on whether he may have been confused on other matters without focussed question on that, because there is always a possibility to --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, let me ask --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- be confused or to have some doubts as the accuracies. So let's really try to focus, I would say, especially with this witness on what we know as facts and find out what he knows for a fact. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pasic, I'm wondering, given the fact that you couldn't identify, in my submission, what Mr. Cigoj looks like and what Mr. Matic looks like, how it is that you know whether there was a concert or whether you were actually present at such a concert of either Mr. Cigoj or Mr. Matic?

utterances.speaker: PETAR PASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can confirm with certainty that I did not attend that concert. When I said that there were several concerts and that there were also single appearances, I thought and I meant concerts in the officers' hall of the Croatian Army. There was a separate appearance by Krunoslav Cigoj and another one by Hrid Matic, and as for this particular event, this particular concert, it was probably an appearance by several performance all at the same time. But I did not attend that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I ask that this video be marked and I tender it into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The 17 seconds, I take it, instead of the two hours, Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, can I ask that the witness take his earphones off, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you take your earphones off for a second.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, in light of the fact that I anticipate a potential argument of discriminatory intent by General Gotovina on the basis of Jure and Boban, I would prefer that the entire two hours be admitted so that we can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So that the Chamber can watch for two hours that Mr. Gotovina is not present or -- well, in opera it is always difficult to know who actually is present. I invite the parties to seek agreement on the fact, whether this video demonstrates in any way the presence at this moment - that's the 17th of August - the presence of any of the accused. And the Chamber is not very much inclined to take a magnifying glass and watch for two hours and see among the huge audience, which we saw before, who is present and who is not present.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I could just state General Forand already testified that he was present at this concert. Mr. Liborius testified that he was present at this concert, and there is no dispute that General Gotovina was present for this concert --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: -- because, as you can see it was also broadcast on national television. From our perspective, it's the presence of the persons and what songs were sung, and it is our position and the reason we're tendering the whole two-hour video is that Jure i Boban is not part of that repertoire.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If that is the issue, then the parties are invited to watch the two hours to see whether this song at this concert was sung, yes or no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If I may just add.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: The next series of questions for the witness is -- we have actually broken down and listed out every song that was sung on the two hours, and now I'm going to ask him which of the songs does he think is a quote/unquote Ustasha song. But I can let the Prosecution then verify.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That makes sense if the Prosecution was referring to the specific concert. If not -- Ms. Gustafson.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, no, the evidence of the witness has been that he wasn't at this concert. The concerts he is referring to were not concerts at the Knin fortress. They were concerts at the HV Dom. Whether or not a Ustasha song is sung at this concert, I don't think has any relevance to the evidence of this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: That is incorrect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I then understand that it's not in dispute that during this concert that the songs you asked questions about were not sung?

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: I would have to review video, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: I have no idea.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand that, but are you willing to seek agreement on this matter?

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: I would be happy to review it and try to seek agreement with Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, Mr. Misetic, are there any songs sung here of which one could even think about whether they would be Ustasha songs, because then it makes perhaps sense to do it. But if the aim of the exercise is to establish that there were none, then I would suggest that you give a list of the songs you think that were sung to Ms. Gustafson so that she can quickly consult with her musical experts to find out whether there is any dispute, yes or no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I just asked, not because I think there was or were any Ustasha songs or anything that could be considered that, but I wanted to also check because the witness mentioned a few other songs in his testimony in answer to Ms. Gustafson, to see whether they were sung at this concert. I don't believe they were. But in any event, Mr. President, the issue here is: A, the witness is present in the courtroom and we wish to confirm or put to the witness some of these matters. Second, with respect to the relevance of it, we think it is relevant because the witness has provided no foundation for any of these concerts and in fact confused and couldn't identify the singers when shown --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If I could just finish, Mr. President. The witness can't identify the singers by sight so I'm wondering and we will challenge that there were such concerts in the HV hall or that the witness was present at such concerts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me ... first and then perhaps may -- I'd like the -- the witness to be asked whether, during these other concerts, the singers were also in costume, yes or no, which might make a difference. What I'm seeking is that we do not spend ages and ages on a matter which I wouldn't say is without relevance, but, at the same time, whether it deserves that much attention. And let's try to identify where the real dispute is, and that seems to be not primarily on this concert but, rather, on what the witness may have seen and heard elsewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I will try that, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I just wish to state for the record I agree with you, but given the amount of time that was spent in cross on Jure i Boban and the issues of discriminatory intent by the accused on the basis of that song, I think that's the reason that I'm going through this in detail. The second is that in terms of the rights to the defendant, we are able to verify where General Gotovina was at various times, and therefore, the failure of the Prosecution to actually establish any foundation for this either through this witness or through the record throughout this trial of any such concerts puts as at a disadvantage, and I do believe that I need to put that to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, just on the foundation point. The foundation is the evidence of this witness that he attended these concerts. There is a foundation for this. I don't understand the allegation that this lacks a foundation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If the witness testifies that he has been present at a certain occasion where some matters -- some songs were sung, then I can imagine, Mr. Misetic, that if the witness would have no clear recollection as to when it exactly was, because the where seems to have been answered by the witness, then I can imagine that you would consider this lack of knowledge on the dates to be relevant for your defence, whereas, Ms. Gustafson may take a different position.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: There was evidence on the dates as well. At page 22844, he thought these events took place in September and August.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I think, as a matter of fact, that if Mr. Misetic is referring to the whereabouts of Mr. Gotovina, that he is not dealing with two months as one unit but, rather, to have a day by day. I do agree with you that the witness was clear and that it was during these two months, and Mr. Misetic thinks that lack of knowledge as to the precise dates may have an impact on the evaluation of the evidence. That is apparently the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: That is correct, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: My point was simply that I do want to go through, just like Ms. Gustafson, when the witness says the 4th and the 7th Guards Brigades were not involved, you go through the who, what, when, where, and why, and that's what I'd like to go through with this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's keep it very factual. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pasic, at these concerts that you say took place in the Croatian Army hall, do you recall whether Mr. Cigoj or Mr. Matic would wear costumes in their performances?

utterances.speaker: PETAR PASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the Croatian Army hall, as far as I recall, I don't think there were in costumes; they were in suits.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And do you remember when these concerts took place?

utterances.speaker: PETAR PASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say exactly. I think some took place in August, others in September, and after that time, I don't think there were any.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Do you recall ever being present at any type of concert with General Gotovina anywhere else other than the HV army hall?

utterances.speaker: PETAR PASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would like to show a video-clip. This is 65 ter 1D2989.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] ... to ask you how many hours it is but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: It's a short -- short clip.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: "THE INTERPRETER: [Voiceover] In Knin today, a Little Christmas Concert was held with performances of children's choirs, ballet and musical groups. "In the season of holiday giving, charity and love, the concert Peace and Love in Knin's Kralj Zvonimir school, sincere greetings were expressed by the youngest ones. Around 400 participants in the Little Christmas Concert consisting of children's choirs, dance and folklore groups from Knin, Split, Zadar, Imotski, Sinj, Sibenik, and Trilj, created a true Christmas spirit at Knin's Kralj Zvonimir school. The Little Christmas Concert was held under the auspices of Ankica Tudjman, president of the humanitarian charity Save the Children of Croatia. The playful and exuberant participants were welcomed by Sibenik's bishop, Dr. Srecko Badurina; Split Military District commander, General Ante Gotovina; and the government's commissioner for Knin, Petar Pasic."

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Does that refresh your recollection, Mr. Pasic, about attending a Christmas concert -- sorry.

utterances.speaker: PETAR PASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, 100 per cent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please repeat your question. We had to wait for the translation to be finished.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pasic, does that refresh your recollection about attending a Little Christmas Concert where both you and General Gotovina were present?

utterances.speaker: PETAR PASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Were any Ustasha songs sung at this children's Christmas concert?

utterances.speaker: PETAR PASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I ask that this exhibit be marked. I tender it into evidence, and I would like to tender the short clip of the Knin castle video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Gustafson.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: I have no objection to this last video. I do object to the Knin castle video on the basis that it has no relevance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think that's a frivolous objection. Obviously we take a different view than the Prosecution concerning where and when General Gotovina was present. Given that it's clearly relevant if the Chamber were to view the evidence in our favour that there were two concerts and these were the two, and there's only two concerts where any presence by my client can be verified, then the Chamber should be able to review what was actually sung. And, moreover, the clip was put to the witness concerning his identification of the two singers. I don't see any basis for a relevance objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The video-clip of the 17th of August will be marked for identification. And the Chamber repeats its urgent invitation to the parties to see what is there, in that video, the parties could agree upon. That is, primarily, then, on whether any Ustasha songs were sung during these two hours. If the parties cannot agree on that, they may address the Chamber jointly and to explain what the songs are that are contested as to their character. The second video-clip, the Christmas concert, the Chamber takes it, for the time being, that Christmas songs were sung there. Mr. Registrar, could you assign numbers.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Knin castle video, 17th August, which is 1D2987, becomes Exhibit D1717, marked for identification. The subsequent video is 1D2989, and that becomes Exhibit D1718.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Misetic, the portion played is the whole of the video, D1718?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: It's from an evening newscast. That is whole of that news, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. D1718 is admitted into evidence. And the Chamber would like to hear from the parties on D1717. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. In light of the Chamber's invitation to the parties, I would like to put the list of the songs to the witness just so I have something on the record in terms of his opinion of the nature of the songs. With the Court's leave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The songs of the 17th of August?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes. I just fear if we get into a dispute later about the nature of the songs, I would like to have the witness provide his opinion while he is here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You would like to have his opinion on the character of the songs that were sung in his absence. Is this a matter of --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I think he would have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- fact or is it a matter of opinion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I believe he has knowledge of the songs outside of the fact that were also sung at this concert. Mr. President, these are very common songs that most -- the average person in Croatia would probably be familiar with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And that's, of course, the main reason for my concern that we start a -- a wide discussion on the character of those songs. Ms. Gustafson.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, there is -- in evidence there are very small number of names of songs. I don't think it will assist the proceedings in any way to list songs that's no evidence on the record of them and then have the opinion of this witness on whether or not it is an Ustasha song.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I suggest the following. The list of songs sung during the 17th of August concert may be provided to the witness so that can he read the list during the next break, and he will then be invited to tell us whether there's any song he considers a Ustasha song or a strong patriotic song, and then we'll hear from him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pasic, I'd like to turn to a different topic now. You heard you'll have some work during the break. My topic now is your -- the circumstances surrounding your 2002 interview with the Prosecution, so if I may ask you a few questions about that. In answer to a question from Ms. Gustafson this morning, you said that some of the words and views expressed in that 2002 statement were the words of the investigator or the interpreter and not your own words. And my question is: When Mr. Foster, who was the investigator, was interviewing you, did he say things to you like, What is your opinion about something; or did he tell you what his opinion of something was and ask you whether you agree with him?

utterances.speaker: PETAR PASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Occasionally he put forth his opinion, and occasionally he asked me for my opinion. When I go back to your previous question, or, rather, we've been discussing extensively the Ustasha songs. I can only repeat that in my interview I did not say Ustasha songs and I had -- I said patriotic songs. Therefore, that term was introduced by him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm going to turn your attention to a different sentence that appear in that 2002 statement, and we've already gone over it but let me ask it again. It's at page 8 of the statement. Where what's written down in the statement is: "I believe that the looting and destruction that took place was planned from above." Now, did Mr. Foster say that he believed that it was planned from above and ask you whether you agree with him; or did you volunteer an opinion that you believed it was planned from above?

utterances.speaker: PETAR PASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that he said that it was planned from above and then sought to hear my opinion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Before the break, I'd like to show you a video-clip --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic, could I ask -- When he sought your opinion on it, did you then expression agreement or disagreement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Firstly I agreed. That is why I said I wanted to make the changes, because they do not correspond to my current thinking and position in relation to the time when I gave the interview.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So what is written down, although in the questions suggested by Mr. Foster actually reflects what you said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not quite accurately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I think - but I may have been -- not be clear, I think that I said "actually" reflects what you said rather than "accurately," which is a -- I may not have pronounced my words with sufficient precision. But do I understand that on this matter, Mr. Foster gave his opinion, asked whether you agreed, and that you, at the time, said that you did agree, although you now tell us that you -- your current thinking is different from what you said at the time. Is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pasic, now following up on that, did Mr. Foster, after you would express agreement with a proposition that he put out there, did he then follow up and say, Mr. Pasic, now let's go and establish the bases, the factual bases for your agreement? For example, on this point about whether crimes were planned from above, did he ask you how do you know that; did you attend a meeting with people from above, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: PETAR PASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: There's other portions where you say, Commanders could have stopped crimes. Did he ask you how do you know that; what is your factual basis for saying such a thing; did you attend meetings with military commanders? Any types of questions like that?

utterances.speaker: PETAR PASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot recall exactly, but as for any meetings with military commanders, be it before or during the military police operation, I did not attend any.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, if you told Mr. Foster that, in fact, you had never attended a meeting of military commanders, or let's assume you said, I don't have any factual basis for my opinion --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic, the witness clearly misunderstood your last question. So let's first try to get an answer to that before we continue and may end up in the realm of speculation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, I thought he answered it by saying, I cannot recall exactly, but I'll follow up with him again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I understood that in view of the remainder of his answer and that's where I -- perhaps we could first try to find out that out. In your statement, you are reported to have said, Commanders could have stopped crimes. Now, first question: Was this something that was suggested or proposed by Mr. Foster to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it was his opinion. I said -- actually, I did not say that the unit commanders were those who could have prevented crimes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, did he then suggest to you in his question that that was the case?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That was his assumption. My opinion --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, okay. Yes, what did you then say? He asked you whether you agreed or not with that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know if I said yes or no. But I think I said no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Do you know anything about follow-up questions in relation to this specific subject; that is, whether the military commanders could have stopped the crimes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think he only wanted to learn from me the names of certain unit commanders, or the units that were in the area. I did respond partially because I knew some of the units and commanders who, at the time, were in Knin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes. Just a last question before the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pasic, if in fact had you been asked by Mr. Foster what your basis of knowledge was for what military commanders could or couldn't have done in that circumstance, when you were reviewing your statement, particularly when it was being read back to you in 2002, would you have asked why those answers concerning your knowledge weren't included in the statement, if you understand what I'm asking?

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm confused by the question. The statement was read back to him in 2002.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: That's my point, Mr. President. If in fact Mr. Foster had asked foundational questions for these opinions, there's an issue that is going to be raised by the Defence as to why Mr. Foster didn't include --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but let's be, then, simple. Was your statement read back to you in 2002?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I told him I didn't understand English, and when I gave that statement, I don't think it was read back to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When I came to sign the second time round, then it was read back to me from English into Croatian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You would say that would have been early 2003. So your statement was -- let me.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour, that was 2002.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I'm sorry, I'm making a mistake in the year. So the statement was read back to the witness, at least that's his testimony. Mr. Misetic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm now about to play a video-clip so it might take between five and ten minutes. I don't know how you wish to proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I further inquire with the parties, as far as the time expectations are concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would say at least another 30 to 45 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And as far as the other Defence teams are concerned. Mr. Mikulicic, still the same situation, no questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I will only have a couple of questions, Your Honour, not more than ten minutes altogether. Even less.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Kay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I won't be more than 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, which means that we will not conclude the testimony today. Mr. Pasic, we will first have a break, and we'll resume at ten minutes to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pasic, during the break have you had a chance to review the songs that were sung on the 17th of August at the Knin castle?

utterances.speaker: PETAR PASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't listen to them. I just looked at the titles and I can tell that I am familiar with all of them. Your question is probably going to be -- but there is not a single one. All these songs express a patriotic feeling without any hint of an insult made against others or another.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. The more specific question is: Would you -- in one of your prior answers you said with respect to Jure i Boban some people might consider that an Ustasha song but you wouldn't. With respect to any of these songs, would some people consider those to be Ustasha songs but you don't? Let me -- let me ask it a different way. Are those -- do those songs have anything to do with the independent state of Croatia or Ustasha, as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: PETAR PASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, nothing whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much for those answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, the next --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Gustafson.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt. I just didn't -- we haven't received a list of the songs, so I'm sure we'll get it in -- oh.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: It's the surrogate sheet to the admitted exhibit. If you open it up, the list is in there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, now we -- I have explored ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have explored the manner in which the OTP statement was taken. I'd like to show the witness now a video of another interview taken by the same OTP investigator on the same topic, which is a plan to expel Serbs, burn their property, et cetera. And I understand from Ms. Gustafson during the break that she has an observation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Gustafson.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I understand that Mr. Misetic intends to tender a portion of the suspect interview of Mr. Jarnjak. I don't see any foundation for that. Mr. Misetic can ask this witness about the questions he was asked in his interview, and to then put another interview -- portion of another interview to him with another person, I don't think has any relevance. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could we first ask the witness to take his earphones off. Yes, Mr. Misetic, let me first give you an opportunity to respond.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes. First, I haven't tendered anything, so at this point it's a premature objection, if it's to the tendering of the video. I intend to explore, though, the methodology of how the statement was taken. The Chamber, I am certain, is familiar with the Tribunal's case law, which the Chamber raised on Friday. With respect to the admissibility for the truth of the matter asserted of the 2002 statement, one of the critical factors taken into account by the Limaj Trial Chamber was the fact that the methodology used by the OTP investigator could be verified because it was videotaped, and the Chamber could explore the reliability of the statement because it was videotaped and the nature and way in which questions were posed. In this case, one of the issues we will be arguing later is that there it no videotape of the interview of this witness for the Chamber to explore the reliability of the way in which the statement was taken. The second issue is that the OTP itself didn't call this witness, and so we will be challenging whether the OTP believes that the 2002 statement is reliable. The third issue is that it's the same investigator on the video we wish to show him posing questions on the exact same topic, which is covered in the 2002 statement and for which no foundation -- I should say no foundation one way or the other, meaning no indication is given in the 2002 statement that Mr. Foster asked the witness what his basis of knowledge was and no indication whether the witness said, I have a basis of knowledge for this or I don't have a basis of knowledge for this. And we believe that the Chamber is entitled to explore with this witness the methodology employed by Mr. Foster, and if there's going to be a debate about whether Mr. Foster uses these types of techniques with witnesses, we are entitled to put to the Chamber the techniques that Mr. Foster has used in the past with other witnesses for which we have a video record of it. And I'm entitled to explore with the witness whether some of the answers or conclusions were, quote/unquote, the words of Mr. Foster and not the witness, which he's already testified about. And also to put the video of the Jarnjak suspect interview into evidence not for the truth of the matters that are discussed on the video but simply for impeachment purposes and to challenge the methodology employed by the Office of the Prosecutor investigators because I suspect this is a factor that the Chamber will have to consider in determining the way in which the 2002 statement will be used. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic, the witness has testified that at various instances matters were put to him as a proposition and that he was asked whether or not he agreed or did not agree. The witness further testified that he is unaware of any follow-up question, specifically in relation to the commanders. He said something that questions were asked, who were the commanders, but which I do not consider a real follow-up question on the matter. Now, what is this video going to add, apart from confirming what the witness said? That's my first -- because now you said the witness was not called by the -- that was your second argument. Was not called by the Prosecution. Therefore, you would -- for that, I take it the issue of reliability of not being called, et cetera, that that's not an issue which would -- which would urge to us look at the video, because calling or not calling can have, I would say, a hundred reasons. And the third issue is same topping and no questions to create a further foundation. That's already what the witness testified. So I'm wondering what this video is going add to what is already the evidence given by this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, the relevance is that -- let me address it this way. If the Prosecution is now going to claim that the 2002 statement is credible and that these are the views of the witness himself, then it becomes a he said, he said between Mr. Foster and Mr. Pasic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If that's the case, then this video bolsters, in our view, Mr. Pasic's assertions that this is how Mr. Foster conducted the interview with him. And we would submit that under Rule 89, this evidence is probative in the sense that it goes to how Mr. Foster conducted interviews of persons within the Croatian system concerning the existence of a plan to expel Serbs, to burn their property, and to loot their property.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Wouldn't then be the next logical step also to verify whether Mr. Foster ever put anything on paper which is inconsistent with what that witness apparently had said. Because there is a multiple claim by this witness. It is sometimes, I didn't say that; and sometimes, I did say that but I've since then changed my mind. Now, for the first portion, if you would say, We'd like to see the methodology of Mr. Foster, that would then include the whole thing. That is, how questions were put to the witness, what was then put on paper, although this is video recorded, so to that extent, there not a lot of margin to -- to reflect answers in any way different from what was literally said. But --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I must admit I'm a bit confused. Is there anything that Mr. Foster put on paper during the interview with this witness? Is that what we're say?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. What I was saying is that if we are exploring the methods used by Mr. Foster, that that goes from the way in which he puts the questions to the witnesses and what then appears on paper. Now, I do see that there is a difference, that if it is recorded, that you will most likely get everything on paper, transcribed and translated. So to that extent, it is -- the situation is quite different. I'm aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And if I can also state, Mr. President, one of the issues I raised before the break, which will be our argument later, is that if in fact Mr. Foster had explored or if the witness had volunteered some of these conclusions, it is our submission that, given that Mr. Foster is a professional investigator, he would have explored the foundations for some of these conclusions that are littered throughout the 2002 statement. And if in fact he did explore, as a professional investigator would have, then those answers to those foundational questions would have been or should have been included in the 2002 statement, even if the witness said, I believe there was a plan but I have no personal knowledge that would support my conclusion on this, I never attended a meeting where anything of the sort was discussed, et cetera. That is what should have happened if, in fact, these questions were put. We suggest, in fact, that the witness is correct, that these conclusions were, in fact, put to him as Mr. Foster's conclusions and that the witness was asked, Do you agree or do you disagree. You were -- and if you watch the video of the Jarnjak interview, the way Mr. Foster says it is, You're a person on the inside, you must know this was -- this is true, although we submit you, Mr. Jarnjak, weren't part of plan. I want to explore with the witness whether, in fact, such techniques were used with this witness to say, You must know the plan existed, this is our view, but we believe you weren't part of the plan, Mr. Pasic.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I could respond briefly. If that is indeed what Mr. Misetic wants to do, to explore with the witness whether these techniques were used with him, he can ask him those questions. He doesn't need to show him the video. Secondly, the -- the suggestion that Mr. Foster would have or should have followed up and would have or should have included things in the 2002 statement, appears to be approaching some kind of allegation of misconduct which we, of course, categorically reject. Mr. Foster is a professional investigator. There are many reasons why investigators do or don't ask follow-up questions to certain conclusions that witnesses give them during interviews. And lastly, Your Honour, what Mr. Misetic said earlier, which is that in his view this video bolsters, in our view, Mr. Pasic's assertions -- that this is how Mr. Foster conducted the interview with him. And we would submit that under Rule 89, this evidence is probative, sounds to me like that is a matter for submissions, that there is nothing to be gained from showing this video to this witness and seeking some kind of conclusion from this witness as to whether it was similar or not. Mr. Misetic can ask the questions about how the interview was conducted. He can make submissions, if and when the opportunity arises, as to what happened -- what may have happened in other interviews and whether or not that's similar. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, just a brief response? I'd --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Very brief.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Ms. Gustafson's argument actually walks right into what my point is. She wasn't present at the 2002 interview. She has no idea how Mr. Foster conducted the interview, yet she tells the Chamber they categorically reject any allegation of misconduct. Now I didn't allege misconduct, but I also wonder what basis Ms. Gustafson has to say there was or wasn't or -- if she knows more about this interview and how it was conducted then appears in the statement itself, then that needs to be disclosed to us. The second point, Mr. President, is that's precisely why we wish to show the Chamber that this sort of veil that, because he's an OTP investigator there's a presumption that everything was done by the book, is exactly the reason why we wish to, A, put this video to the witness; and B, let the Chamber decide for itself whether this issue needs to be explored even further.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, the allegations that Mr. Misetic is making are based on this witness's evidence which is confused and contradictory. This witness has impeached himself on the way that this interview was conducted. And for Mr. Misetic now to make allegations against Mr. Foster on that basis is not well founded. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I need the record to be clear --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, Mr. Misetic. There was an objection. You've responded to that, then, yes, you are the last one to -- because you're the attacked party in this respect --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- but please keep it short.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: It's very short. I never made any allegation against Mr. Foster. I'm interested in exploring the matter with Mr. Pasic first, before allegations are made. Secondly, if there's nothing wrong with how the Jarnjak video was conducted, and I'm not suggesting that that is misconduct because it was in fact videotaped, but techniques used by investigators don't have to amount to misconduct to -- to nevertheless call into question the reliability of statements made during an interview. It's not misconduct if -- if techniques were used that make certain statements in a statement unreliable. And to that extent, I wish to reiterate I have not made any allegations against Mr. Foster. I am exploring with the witness the methodology used by the investigator which he --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which is repetitious.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: -- used in other cases.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's repetitious.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: But which he used in other cases.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In view of the testimony of the witness until now, the Chamber does not consider it the best way to proceed to show to the witness what happened in this interview with Mr. Jarnjak. At the same time, the Chamber considers that there could be good reasons to explore what happened. The Chamber would like to proceed in the following way. The Chamber would like to look at a selection, Mr. Misetic, you will play so that the Chamber is better aware of techniques you are apparently referring to. This not to be shown to the witness at this moment. We'll ask him to leave the courtroom. Then the Chamber invites you and the Chamber may even take some initiative in exploring the matters without having shown, still, the video to the witness to see whether similar techniques or whether the interview was conducted in a similar way without leading the witness. And then, at that point in time, we'll see whether it makes any sense to show then to the witness the video or not. So the Chamber would like to take this step-by-step approach. Therefore, agreeing with you that it is worthwhile exploring, but the way in which it is done is a different one than you suggest.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: That's fine, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Pasic, we would like to proceed I don't know exactly how many minutes, but to proceed briefly without your presence. I therefore invite you to follow Madam Usher, and we'd like to see you back most likely very soon. So if you could remain standby, that would be good.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic, may I take it that you have some selection limited in time which demonstrates the techniques used.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: That's what I am discussing right now with my Case Manager, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, just one question. This is a suspect interview so there is a simultaneous translation within the video itself. I leave it to Your Honour as to whether the booths need to be simultaneously interpreting or whether we should just let the video play.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps it is even good to know exactly how the questions were translated and not have a kind of a -- which allows always to see whether there are any translation issues involved here. I hope, Mr. Misetic, that, unlike with the interviews given by Mr. Cermak, that we do not have untranslated portions or untranscribed portions. Have you provided transcripts to the booth?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, we have, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And your selection is now known to the booth as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: It is not yet, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But I take it that you will then clearly announce what you will play so that the booth can find the relevant portions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: With the consent of the parties, I suggest that we do not receive additional translation from our booth, because, finally, this enables the Chamber to exactly follow the information as it was given at the time to the -- to the investigators.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. President, then I will call out the clip. It is 65 ter 1D2988. And for the benefits of the interpreters, we will start from the very beginning, so page 1 of that clip. And we will go to the top of the third page of the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And sounds quality is such that --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I believe it's good.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: "AP: But they were so big, they were of the opinion that the policemen were just there to disturb them. What is he ... what is he here, to stop him during the night! "And it was difficult for me, because of that ... for these men were professionals, who were just doing their job. "BF: Which is why I say that ... we will say that there was an agenda, a different agenda ... an agenda where certain elements of the military, and even the special police, were used ... to ensure that all Serbs in the liberated area were removed ... and those who were left behind were killed ... and their property destroyed ... so that they would not be able to return. And this is why you were getting no communication between your organisation and the military. This is why the Ministry of Defence didn't want to give you any assessment of what was caused by the conflict and what was caused by other means. This is why your civilian policemen, despite their professionalism, were not succeeding in preventing or prosecuting the serious crimes that occurred. This is what we say was happening, and it seems from what you say ... yours is an explanation as to how it could happen, because of this wall, this wall of silence, this difficulty in coordination. "AP: But this difficulty did not exist only during Storm. That was the approach from the very beginning. Because the Croatian Army had a lot of generals in the beginning from the former JNA ... and their philosophy was: Civilians can only go to that military wall and they can go anywhere, and that was so from the very first day, 1991, as far as I can remember. And it's not about a special agenda they had for these operations. And it was, I have to say that, on the ground, an idiot ... idiots or former of members, active members, of the Croatian Army ... criminals who were dressed up in uniforms of the Croatian Army ... there were cases of personal revenge ... because on that ... in that area from 1992 to 1995, 650 Croats were killed. They came back after five years ... and, of course, there were many cases of personal revenge. "BF: I understand the plight of the returnees, and I understand that many of them certainly would have committed crimes on their return ... but we have a great deal of evidence showing identified military units killing, burning, destroying and looting during the course of all three operations, running from Medak, Flash, and Storm. "So it's all right what you say, it wasn't just Storm. There was a plan to recover and liberate the occupied territory ... to remove the Serbs and re-house Croats ... and make sure that it was very difficult, if not impossible, for the Serbs who had lived there for many, many years, to return. And I think you were aware, as a result of the many meetings that you attended ... that these plans were afoot. I'm not suggesting that you were part of those plans ... because I think there are difficulties with this communication and the fact that certain people were allowed to be within the inner circle, and others were not. But I am satisfied that you were certainly aware that this was a plan and this had successfully occurred in the Medak Pocket operation ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: There's a second clip, Mr. President, if we could just play the second clip.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: There's about one minute left. It begins at the bottom of page 2 of the -- or page 1 of the second clip.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: "AP: I reject any possibility that I ever knew about any such plan and, in particular, that I was a part of this plan, because why would I take all these actions had I known about a plan" --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: That's the excerpt, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Usher, could you please escort the witness into the courtroom. Before we continue, the video starts with "We will say this, and it seems that what you are saying is," that it's unclear to the Chamber to what extent this summarises part of the earlier answers given by that witness, because if you say it seems what you say, you can just imagine what the suspect would say, but it also could be that it in one way or other summarises what he has said already. That's a bit unclear. And I take it you will have an opportunity to check that, Ms. Gustafson, and Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I can -- yes. We had to make a selection and, Mr. President, the Chamber has heard other evidence on this same point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I'm not asking -- I'm not asking to present it all to the Chamber, but in all fairness, it's an observation I'd like to make. I would have a few questions for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Pasic, we are -- we will be talking about how this interview with the investigator of the Prosecution actually took place. Now, you told us earlier that sometimes matters were proposed to you, and I specifically refer, for example, whether the commanders could have stopped the crimes. Now, if such a thing was proposed to you, in what way was that done? Would they say, Isn't it true that the commanders could put an end; or would they say, The Prosecution thinks that, it's our position that we could -- that the commanders could have stopped these crimes. Which -- could you tell us a bit more in detail what exactly then was proposed and in what terms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The first part of what you said is correct, when you asked how and in what way. It was, as you explained. That was their method of work.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I explained it in two different ways. The one being that they would say to you, This is what happened. Do you agree --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The first possibility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So they -- did they ever say, We, the investigators -- as investigators, we think that it was done this way, and would you please comment on that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As I said, partially they put questions as well as offered answers, or led answers. When I see it now, and I hope I won't upset you, but to me, it seems that the level of questions is of low standard. It doesn't correspond to my intelligence, and I don't think it matches the intelligence of those who were putting questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, let's, let's refrain from seeking your qualification of -- of the quality of the questions. What I'm interested in to know, and I ask you again: If they proposed something to you, did they propose that as what their position was, or did they propose it to you just as if these were facts?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was more their position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do I understand your answer correctly: If you say, Well, they put it to me as what they thought was the truth, rather than to present it as an absolute truth of the facts?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. It was more their position rather than an absolute fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, did they, as far as you remember, once you had answered questions, did they ever oppose the two to each other, that is to say, We think this is what happened, and it seems that you are saying that this and this and this is what happened. Is that something that happened during those interviews, as far as you remember?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. The entire interview between us took place in such a way, and only towards the end were the minutes put at my disposal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But if you say: "The entire interview between us took place in such a way," what do you mean exactly by "in such a way"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In such a way that I wasn't told in Croatian what I had said earlier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You would say your statement, up to that moment, was not summarised, and not put in contrast with what their position was. Is that ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, if you had given an answer which might not be consistent with what they thought would have happened, what did they then say to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Nothing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did it happen that you gave answers where they wanted to make clear to you that that was not consistent with what they thought had happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Does that mean that the answers you gave were, in general, in line with what they had put to you as a proposal of what their view and their position was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did they ever raise the issue, when putting questions to you, whether you would have been involved or not been involved in any of -- in any form of any wrong-doings which they may have considered that had taken place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did they ever say to you, Don't hesitate to give the right answer because we're not blaming you for it; or did they ever say, Well, be careful because you might have been involved as well. Was there any -- was there ever any reference to your possible involvement in what they apparently considered wrong behaviour?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, more specifically talking about whether crimes that may have been committed, were committed or not, and whether there was any plan behind that, did they ever allude to others being involved in this planning, not you, or to the contrary, you being involved and others not? Was there ever -- was this matter ever raised when questioning, from, Don't worry, you may not have been part of this planning; or was that ever suggested to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there anything else you would like to bring to our attention in relation to how this interview was conducted, where we know that you have testified that you may not have spoken some of the words and in other respects may have changed your views on the matter. But is there anything else, in relation to these interviews, you think we should be aware of in order to be able to evaluate the statement, as it was put on paper, in addition to what you've told us already?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] By your leave, I would only add that some of the blame is mine to bear as well, for having signed such a statement. I don't want to put all the blame on the investigators.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Judge Gwaunza has a question in relation to this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GWAUNZA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pasic, just carrying on with the -- with the -- with the issue that Judge Orie has been pursuing, when the investigators put, according to your opinion, questions that were leading, did you find it difficult to disagree with them and tell them that they were wrong and then for you to put forward what your position was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was very difficult for me to answer the questions put in such a way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GWAUNZA
utterances.text: Why was it difficult?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because they wanted to receive an answer from me the way I may not have phrased it. They wanted to receive a direct answer to their questions, which not -- would not have necessarily been completely mine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GWAUNZA
utterances.text: Thank you for those answers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And you said that was difficult. But did you, at any moment, resist their suggestions to say, Well, no, you're not right here, this is not how it happened; or, Your position is wrong.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So whatever they asked you, whatever they put to you, you just said, You're right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] More a yes than a no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Pasic, we have not yet concluded your testimony. We have not concluded to hear your testimony, and, therefore, we'd like to see you back tomorrow. And unless there's any procedural issue also in relation to the way in which we proceeded at this very moment, if there is nothing to be raised in that respect, we'll adjourn and we will resume tomorrow, Tuesday, the 13th of October, 9.00 in this courtroom. But, I again would like to instruct you that you should not speak with anyone about your testimony, whether given already or still to be given, also not to discuss whatever the audience may have seen when you were not present.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no one to discuss it with. No one, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Pasic, we'd like to see you back tomorrow at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 13th day of October, 2009, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.48 p.m.,
